It differs from its parent, Gaussian Smoothing for Level-Set Extraction, by using a simpler averaging kernel that is computationally cheaper but may preserve less of the original field's high-frequency detail [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes the algorithm as applying a 'box blur filter' (which is a simpler averaging kernel) to the density field. It details the calculation of the average of the current voxel and its 6 immediate neighbors (a 7-voxel kernel). This process converts binary steps into smooth transitions, which inherently preserves less high-frequency detail (sharp edges) compared to the original binary field, while being computationally simpler than more complex smoothing kernels.
